findings.observation: Sheet 21 labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' shows 4 transformer pads and individual unit meters but contains no evidence of formal coordination with Austin Energy Design. Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains standard AE boilerplate language about easements and tree work, but no documentation of initial coordination meeting. Master Comment Report references AE Design review via Bluebeam with reviewer Rosemary Avila (rosemary.avila@austinenergy.com) and notes that AE completeness check is complete. However, no ESPA (Electric Service Planning Application) correspondence, design meeting notes, or initial coordination documentation found in project files. Plan shows preliminary design only.
findings.reasoning: The plan shows a 'Preliminary' electrical design, indicating formal design review with AE Design has not been completed/approved. While Master Comment Report acknowledges AE Design review process is underway (Bluebeam link provided), no evidence of initial coordination meeting discussing service requirements, loads, transformer locations, routing, meter locations, and facilities was located. The completeness check status shows AE review is pending, not completed. Cannot confirm that initial coordination with AE Design discussing permanent electric service requirements, loads, transformer locations, routing, and meter locations was completed per UCM § 1.4.2.
findings.comment: Initial coordination with AE Design to discuss permanent electric service requirements, projected electrical loads, transformer locations, underground cabling routing, meter locations, and additional required facilities must be documented with AE Design approval before site plan approval.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows service routing with blue line entering from Valley View Road right-of-way on west side, suggesting connection to existing AE infrastructure. However, no explicit documentation found regarding whether line extension is required or not. Master Comment Report references AE Design review via Bluebeam but no ESPA correspondence discussing line extension applicability was located. Engineer's Summary Letter does not address electric service planning. No evidence of AE determination of whether adequate existing facilities exist at proposed service location.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.3.12 requires discussion of line extension requirements with AE Design. The applicability checklist note specifically states 'Note: Line extension applicability cannot be determined from distance alone—requires Austin Energy determination during ESPA review.' Without access to ESPA correspondence or AE Design approval letters discussing whether line extension is required, cannot verify this item was properly addressed. The preliminary plan routing suggests possible service from existing infrastructure, but without formal AE determination document, status remains unclear.
findings.comment: AE Design determination of line extension requirements must be documented in ESPA correspondence and referenced on site plans or in approval correspondence.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 Preliminary Electrical Design Plan shows transformer pads and distribution routing but does not explicitly indicate whether 3-phase service is required or provided. No electrical engineering drawings or load calculations found that would identify 3-phase requirements. No AE Design approval correspondence discussing single-phase vs. 3-phase service determination located. Applicability note states: 'Cannot be inferred from civil plans alone.'
findings.reasoning: The checklist notes that 3-phase service determination requires review of electrical drawings showing 3-phase designation or AE approval correspondence confirming 3-phase requirement. The civil site plan cannot establish this requirement alone. Without electrical engineering drawings or AE Design approval correspondence addressing phase service requirements, cannot determine whether this item applies or has been properly addressed with AE Design.
findings.comment: Three-phase service requirements must be addressed with AE Design in ESPA review. If 3-phase is required, provide AE Design approval correspondence confirming service configuration.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 is labeled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' - explicitly indicating it is preliminary, not formally designed or approved. Master Comment Report (section 02-electric-review.md) references AE Design review via Bluebeam markup but provides only a link to comments (https://studio.bluebeam.com/share/epcafnizivuefw), not approval correspondence. No dated AE Design approval letter, design review completion documentation, or formal approval correspondence was located in supplementary documents. Completeness check shows 'AE completeness check complete' but this is not the same as formal design review approval.
findings.reasoning: The plan is explicitly labeled 'PRELIMINARY' which means the formal design review and approval process with AE Design has not been completed. UCM § 1.4.2 requires preliminary design to be 'formally reviewed and approved by AE Design prior to site plan approval.' Completeness check completion is not the same as design approval. The Master Comment Report acknowledges AE Design review is pending (via Bluebeam comments), but no approval documentation has been provided. This is a clear deficiency - the design is still in preliminary status.
findings.comment: Preliminary electric service design must be formally reviewed and approved by AE Design before site plan approval. Obtain design approval from Austin Energy Design business unit and provide approval correspondence.

findings.observation: No AE Design approval correspondence found in project files. Master Comment Report references Bluebeam review comments link but no approval letter, design review completion letter, or formal correspondence from Austin Energy Design approving the preliminary electrical design was located. Engineer's Summary Letter does not mention electric service. Completeness check results show only that 'AE completeness check complete' from Victor Givens, not design review approval.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2 requires 'Proof of correspondence from AE Design approving preliminary electric design' to be submitted. The absence of any AE Design approval letter, approval correspondence, or signed design review documentation is a direct non-compliance. Completeness check confirmation is an administrative milestone, not design approval. Master Comment Report indicates design review is still pending/in process (Bluebeam comments awaiting response).
findings.comment: Provide correspondence from Austin Energy Design approving the preliminary electrical design. This must include design review approval from AE Design business unit, not just completeness check confirmation.

Without access to the AE Design approval correspondence or meeting notes, cannot compare the plans shown on Sheet 21 against what was discussed and approved with AE staff. findings.reasoning: This item requires comparison of current plans against AE-approved design. findings.comment: Once AE Design approval is obtained, verify that electric layout shown on Sheet 21 matches the design discussed and approved with AE staff.

findings.comment: If this electrical design represents changes from a previously AE-approved design, provide re-coordination and new approval documentation from Austin Energy Design.

findings.comment: Once AE Design approval is obtained, reflect the approved electric service design on the landscape plan (Sheet 31) to show transformer locations, routing, easements, and any impacts on landscaping per UCM § 1.4.2.

applicableAreas: Four transformer pad locations shown on Sheet 21
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four transformer pads located at: (1) west of Building 1, (2) west of Building 8, (3) east of Building 5, and (4) east of Building 6. The pads are depicted as square symbols with callouts 'Electrical Transformer Pad' but no specifications, clearances, dimensions, or design details are shown. No documentation found indicating transformer pad locations and specifications were approved by AE Design. Sheet 21 is labeled preliminary - design not yet approved.
findings.reasoning: This item requires that 'Transformer pad location and specifications not approved by AE Design or not shown on plans as approved.' The pad locations are shown on Sheet 21, but: (1) no design details/specifications are provided, (2) no approval documentation for these specific locations was found, and (3) the design is still preliminary. UCM § 1.10.4 requires AE Design approval of pad locations, clearances, and specifications. Without AE approval correspondence addressing these specific pad locations and specifications, cannot confirm compliance.
findings.comment: Obtain AE Design approval of all transformer pad locations, specifications, and required clearances per UCM § 1.10.4. Provide design details (dimensions, setbacks, access requirements) on Sheet 21 as approved by AE Design.

applicableAreas: Eight building locations - individual unit meter locations shown on Sheet 21
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows eight individual 'Electrical Meters' callouts (one for each building). Vision analysis indicated these appear to be individual unit meters (gang meters). However, no documentation found indicating meter locations were discussed with or approved by AE Metering Group. UCM § 1.9.3 requires meters be: (1) outdoors, (2) readily accessible, (3) on first floor/ground level, (4) within sight of AE transformer. No details provided on Sheet 21 showing that these meter locations meet these requirements. No approval correspondence from AE Metering Group located.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires 'Meter locations not approved by AE Metering Group per UCM § 1.9.3.' While meters are shown on Sheet 21, no evidence was found that: (1) AE Metering Group reviewed and approved these locations, or (2) the meter locations comply with UCM § 1.9.3 requirements (outdoor, accessible, first floor, within sight of transformer). For a multi-unit development, individual unit meters need specific AE approval of locations. This is a deficiency.
findings.comment: Obtain approval from AE Metering Group for all meter locations per UCM § 1.9.3. Verify each meter is: (1) outdoors, (2) readily accessible, (3) on first floor/ground level, (4) within sight of the AE transformer, and (5) not in prohibited locations (under porches, under overhangs >72 inches, within 3-foot radius of gas meters). Provide detailed meter location plans and AE approval correspondence.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing with blue lines indicating 'Underground Electric Line.' No specific duct bank specifications, materials, sizes, or design details are shown. No documentation found indicating duct bank design was discussed or approved by AE Design. The design is preliminary and unapproved.
findings.reasoning: This item requires 'Underground electric duct bank locations and design not meeting AE requirements or not approved.' While routing is shown on Sheet 21, no duct bank design specifications are provided, and no AE Design approval was found. Once AE Design approval is obtained, duct bank specifications must be verified to meet AE requirements.
findings.comment: Provide underground electric duct bank specifications and locations on Sheet 21 and obtain AE Design approval per UCM § 1.4.2. Include duct bank materials, sizing, installation details, and protection requirements.

Vision analysis noted 'Electrical Pull Box' callouts on the drawing, but no detailed specifications, locations, or design documentation provided. No AE Design approval of manhole specifications located.
findings.reasoning: This item requires 'Electric service manhole locations and design not meeting AE requirements or not approved.' While pull boxes are referenced on Sheet 21, no specifications or AE Design approval documentation was found. Once AE approval is obtained, manhole/pull box design must be verified against AE requirements.
findings.comment: Provide detailed specifications and locations for all electric service pull boxes and any required vaults per AE Design requirements. Include design details and obtain AE Design approval per UCM § 1.4.2.

applicableAreas: Underground electric routing shown on Sheet 21
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing with blue lines and callouts 'Underground Electric Line' connecting from the property boundary inward to transformer pads and service points. However, no detailed routing specifications, cable types, depths, clearances from other utilities, or design requirements are shown. No AE Design approval of routing was found. Design is preliminary.
findings.reasoning: This item requires verification that 'Underground electric cabling routing not meeting AE design requirements or not approved.' Sheet 21 shows general routing paths, but without detailed design specifications and AE approval, cannot confirm routing meets AE requirements for clearances, cable types, depths, and other specifications per UCM § 1.4.2.
findings.comment: Provide detailed underground electric routing specifications including cable types, conduit requirements, depths, clearances from other utilities, and road crossings. Obtain AE Design approval of routing per UCM § 1.4.2.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows four transformer pads but provides no clearance dimensions or specifications. Vision analysis indicated pads are positioned: (1) west of Bldg. 1, (2) west of Bldg. 8, (3) east of Bldg. 5, and (4) east of Bldg. 6. No measurements or setback distances shown. No documentation found indicating clearance reductions were discussed with or approved by AE Design. Standard AE requirements are 10-15 feet hot-stick area, 5 feet sides with operators, 3 feet other sides.
findings.reasoning: This item requires verification that non-standard clearances (if applicable) have written AE Design approval per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 2. Without clearance dimensions shown on the plans and no AE approval of any non-standard configurations, cannot verify compliance. Need detailed transformer pad location drawings showing all clearances and dimensions relative to buildings, property lines, utilities, and landscaping.
findings.comment: Provide detailed transformer pad location and clearance drawings showing all dimensions, setbacks from buildings, property lines, utilities, and landscaping per UCM § 1.10.4 standards. If any clearance reductions are proposed, provide written approval from AE Design per UCM § 1.10.4 footnote 2.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows service entry from the west (Valley View Road right-of-way) with blue 'Underground Electric Line' entering the property, suggesting connection to existing AE infrastructure in/near the right-of-way. However, the plans do not clearly label or delineate existing AE duct banks, underground infrastructure, or service locations. Sheet 9 and Sheet 21 show some existing utilities but existing AE underground infrastructure is not clearly identified and marked.
findings.reasoning: This item requires 'Existing AE underground infrastructure and duct banks not clearly shown on plans' per UCM § 1.16.0. While Sheet 21 shows the service routing entry point, existing AE infrastructure upstream (in Valley View Road and adjacent right-of-way) is not clearly delineated. Need to verify whether existing AE underground facilities and duct banks in the area are clearly marked on the plans.
findings.comment: Clearly identify and mark all existing Austin Energy underground infrastructure and duct banks on Sheet 21 and other relevant utility plans per UCM § 1.16.0. Include existing service locations and connection points.

findings.observation: Sheet 8 is titled 'Tree Removal & Demolition Plan.' The existing facility (demolished June 2022) had electric service that required removal. However, the current site plan sheets do not contain the required callout: 'Contractor to coordinate with Austin Energy on the relocation/removal of the existing electric lines/poles' per UCM § 1.16.0. While prior demolition is complete, any future excavation or construction activities affecting underground utilities must include this coordination note.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.16.0 requires a specific callout on demolition/relocation plans when existing AE facilities require removal or relocation. This callout must be clearly stated on the site plan. Although prior demolition occurred, the current site plan should document that this coordination was/is required. The callout is not present on the reviewed sheets.
findings.comment: Add required callout to demolition/site plan notes: 'Contractor to coordinate with Austin Energy on the relocation/removal of the existing electric lines/poles' per UCM § 1.16.0.

applicableAreas: Entire site - proximity to existing AE transmission easement
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes, Block 20) lists 16 Austin Energy transmission easement requirements with strict clearances and access rules. Block 20 states: 'Do not dig or grade within 25 feet of transmission structures' (items 2, 15); 'Call Andrew Perez at 512-505-7153 to schedule a meeting' (item 2). Transmission poles/structures exist on or near the property based on these detailed requirements. The proposed electric service routing on Sheet 21 must avoid conflicts with transmission easement areas. No documentation found indicating clearance conflicts were discussed and resolved with AE Design prior to site plan approval.
findings.reasoning: This item requires 'Clearance conflicts with existing electric facilities not discussed and resolved with AE Design group prior to site plan approval' per UCM § 1.10.0. The site has existing AE transmission easement areas that require 25-foot clearances and specific access requirements. The new underground routing on Sheet 21 must be verified to avoid conflicts. Without evidence of AE coordination on clearances and transmission easement compatibility, this cannot be confirmed.
findings.comment: Verify that proposed underground electric routing and all construction activities maintain required clearances from existing Austin Energy transmission structures and easement areas per UCM § 1.10.0. Provide documentation of clearance discussion with AE (contact Andrew Perez 512-505-7153 as noted on the plans).

applicableAreas: Demolition of existing facility with electric service
findings.observation: Project involves demolition (facility demolished June 2022 per facts.md). Existing facility was an assisted living center that required electric service, meter, and service drop. No documentation found on current site plan or in supplementary documents confirming: (1) Austin Energy removed the electric meter and service drop before/during demolition, (2) whether site plan sheets include coordination notes for AE removal, or (3) evidence that work request was submitted to AE for removal. Sheet 8 (Demolition Plan) does not clearly document this coordination.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.13 requires that 'Existing electric service, meter, and service drop not coordinated with AE for removal before demolition may proceed.' The regulation requires: (1) written verification that utilities are suitable/sufficient (if continuing), and (2) after demolition approval but before demolition, contact AE to arrange removal. While demolition is already complete (June 2022), the current site plan submittal should document that this coordination occurred. The absence of clear documentation is a deficiency.
findings.comment: Provide documentation that Austin Energy removed the existing electric meter and service drop from the demolished facility before demolition. If not yet removed, submit work request to AE and document the removal per UCM § 1.10.13.

findings.observation: Sheet 12 shows storm sewer plan; Sheet 21 shows electric design with underground routing. Both sheets would need to be examined together to identify potential conflicts between storm drain routing and electric conduit/transmission. Sheet 3 mentions street lighting and transmission easement requirements but no specific documentation found addressing storm drain vs. street light conduit conflicts.
findings.reasoning: This item requires verification that 'Proposed storm drain or utility conflicts with existing street light conduit not discussed with AE Design for resolution' per UCM § 1.13.0. This requires examining both the storm sewer and electric/lighting plans together. Without detailed visual analysis of both sheets and evidence of coordination, cannot confirm resolution of potential conflicts.
findings.comment: Verify that storm drain routing on Sheet 12 does not conflict with underground electric routing and street light conduit on Sheet 21. If conflicts exist, provide documentation of AE Design coordination and approved resolution per UCM § 1.13.0.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric line entering from the west (Valley View Road right-of-way) but does not explicitly label or identify the 'Point of Service' - the demarcation point where Austin Energy responsibility ends and customer responsibility begins. Vision analysis confirmed: 'The exact technical demarcation point where utility responsibility ends and private service begins is not specifically identified by a label.' The point of service is a critical element that must be shown and approved by AE Design.
findings.reasoning: This item requires 'Point of electric service not shown on site plan or not approved by AE Design group' per UCM § 1.4.2. While the service routing is shown, the specific point of service demarcation is not labeled. This is required to be clearly identified on the plan and approved by AE Design. This is a clear deficiency.
findings.comment: Clearly identify and label the Point of Service on Sheet 21 (where Austin Energy facilities end and customer facilities begin). Obtain approval from Austin Energy Design confirming the service point location.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows 8 buildings with individual unit meters (gang meters) for 39 townhome units. Vision analysis confirmed: 'There are eight (8) specific callouts reading..."Electrical Meters." There is one callout pointing to an exterior wall of every single building (Bldgs. 1 through 8)...visual hash marks on those banks roughly correspond to the number of units in that specific building, these appear to be clustered individual unit meters (gang meters).' However, no documentation found indicating: (1) how many individual service drops are provided per unit, (2) whether each unit has its own service drop from the transformer pad, (3) AE approval of individual unit meter configuration for townhome units per AE standards, or (4) whether the design meets AE requirements for individual unit service in multi-unit developments.
findings.reasoning: This item requires 'Each individual unit lacking separate service drop and meter as required by AE standards' per UCM § 1.3.8. While gang meters are shown, AE requires separate service drops for each unit in multi-unit residential developments. The preliminary design shows meters clustered by building but does not document how many service drops are provided or whether AE Design approved individual service drops per unit. Without AE Design approval confirming each unit has a separate service drop and meter per AE standards, this cannot be confirmed as compliant.
findings.comment: Provide documentation from Austin Energy Design confirming that each of the 39 townhome units has a separate service drop and individual meter as required by AE standards per UCM § 1.3.8. Include service drop routing details and AE approval correspondence.

findings.observation: Project is a 39-unit multi-family townhome development under single ownership (WM 41 Austin RE LLC per facts.md and cover sheet). The grouping guidance for unified development states: 'This status cannot be determined from plans alone—requires Austin Energy determination based on ownership, development pattern, and operational characteristics.' No Austin Energy determination letter confirming unified development status was located. The issue of whether future cessation of unified status has been addressed with provisions for individual property service drops is not documented.
findings.reasoning: This item applies 'Only for unified developments (common ownership, integrated operation per AE interpretation).' While the project appears to be single-ownership multi-family development, AE must formally determine if this qualifies as a 'unified development' per their interpretation. If so, provisions for future separate service to individual properties in event of unified development dissolution must be in place. Without AE determination and provisions documentation, this item cannot be confirmed.
findings.comment: If this project is determined by Austin Energy to be a unified development, provide documentation that provisions are included for future separate electric service to individual properties in the event that unified development status is terminated per UCM § 1.3.8.
